name: IIFL Capital Services Ltd
title: IIFL Capital Services Ltd - 542773 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 operational revenue up 20% YoY to INR644 crore, but operational PBT fell 22% for FY26 on employee costs; no capacity or supply signal, and management was evasive on the fundraise and Fairfax stake.

summary.headline: FY26 operational revenue flat at INR2,439 crores as retail fell 9%, while Q4 operational revenue rose 20% YoY to INR644 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 operational revenue was flat YoY at INR2,439 crores, with retail equity revenue down 9% to INR1,121 crores on SEBI regulatory changes that took full-year effect. Institutional and IB revenue rose 11% to INR712 crores and financial product distribution rose 16% to about INR590 crores. Q4 operational revenue grew 20% YoY to INR644 crores and 10% QoQ, but operational PBT fell 22% for the full year on higher employee costs. Management flagged market volatility from geopolitical events, record FPI outflows in March, and an income tax search with about INR56 crores of combined notices under appeal.

segments.name: Retail broking
segments.commentary: FY26 retail equity revenue INR1,121 crores, down 9% on SEBI regulatory changes; Q4 retail revenue INR298 crores, up 22% YoY and 3% QoQ.

segments.name: Institutional broking and investment banking
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR712 crores, up 11%; Q4 about INR162 crores, up from INR97 crores YoY and flat QoQ. Management split the current-period figure roughly as INR450 crores broking and INR250 crores banking.

segments.name: Financial product distribution (FPD)
segments.commentary: FY26 income close to INR600 crores (about INR590 crores), up 16%; Q4 INR182 crores, down 4% YoY on a high prior-year base but up 36% QoQ, driven by insurance and NCD/fixed income placements. FPD AUM about INR52,000 crores.

segments.name: Wealth / HNI channel
segments.commentary: New HNI channel AUM about INR12,000 crores with a product mix similar to the overall book. Around 50 wealth RMs and about 300 affluent/PCG broking RMs.

segments.name: Asset management and manufacturing
segments.commentary: Company has started in-house manufacturing on PMS and AIF platforms (early stage, late stage and credit). Capital Credit Opportunities fund closed, raising about INR500 crores.

guidance_outlook: No explicit FY27 AUM or revenue guidance; management said it has no specific AUM target in mind but must increase assets.
Management expects capital to support about 20% growth over the next couple of years without new capital, per Q&A.
Short-term impact expected from RBI F&O-related margin rules effective 1 July, with marginal direct impact because the company does no prop trading.
Management views the reset of domestic mutual fund yields from 1 April as having a marginal impact on realisations.
Management expects to add wealth RMs in FY27 but gave no number.
capex_capacity: Investments in branches and technology drove depreciation up 20% in FY26 and 6% YoY in Q4 (new branch commissioned).
Finance cost rise tied to working capital needs from MTF book growth.
Net worth grew from about INR1,000 crores to INR3,000-plus crores over four years, entirely from accruals, per management.
Capital deployed mainly in broking, MTF and exchange margins; in-house PMS and AIF manufacturing started.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the sequential MTF book decline to market volatility in the last quarter.

Within total FY26 income of about INR419-420 crores in interest-related income, management said roughly 50% related to MTF and 50% to deposits; MTF interest was about INR160-170 crores, interest expense about INR180 crores.
Clients will bear higher F&O trading costs from the new margin rules.
Q4 FPD jump attributed to insurance and NCD/fixed income placements.
Retail regulatory changes from SEBI, effective in the first quarter of the prior calendar year, caused the full-year retail decline.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FPD AUM growth, and how many RMs were added and planned for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FPD AUM rose from about INR31,000 crores to INR52,000 crores, with growth across MF (INR14,000 to about INR21,000 crores), PMS, AIF and fixed income. About 50 wealth RMs and 300 affluent/PCG RMs; management aims to grow wealth RMs but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the MTF book decline sequentially, and what is the Q4 institutional broking/IB split?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline attributed to market volatility in the last quarter. Institutional revenue roughly INR700 crores split about INR450 crores broking and INR250 crores banking, rough figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is a fund raise planned, and what would the funds be used for?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share details, saying the Board evaluates acquisitions and projects continuously and will disclose when definitive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI rules from 1 July and of MF yield reset from 1 April?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term impact on working capital and margins; marginal impact on the company as it does no prop trading. Yield reset impact seen as marginal since effective yield was already near the regulator's suggested range.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the HNI channel and what is its product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR12,000 crores of AUM through the new HNI channel, with a product mix similar to the overall book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NII/net interest margin, and how is MTF interest split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated net interest spread at about 4% and said MTF and deposit interest split roughly 50-50. Attribution is hard, so the answer was incomplete; the analyst was invited to a follow-up meeting.

qa_highlights.question: Any color on Fairfax stake increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment and said it would disclose once there is something definitive.

qa_highlights.question: Can net worth of about INR3,000 crores support growth, and are new businesses planned such as an AMC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has enough capital for about 20% growth. Core businesses are IB, insurance, equities and wealth management; in-house PMS and AIF manufacturing has started, and new opportunities will be evaluated.

risks_watch: Sustained market volatility and record FPI outflows in March; the trend was said to continue.
Margin and working capital rules from 1 July could hit F&O volumes and client activity.
Employee cost growth (including variable pay) is outpacing revenue, pressuring operational PBT.

Income tax search: about INR56 crores in combined notices for IIFL management and IIFL facilities (block period April 2018 to February 2025); about INR27 crores ad hoc amount paid earlier. Appeals are being filed; no provision made, and the holding company's assessment is still in progress.
Possible capital raise: the analyst asked about a fund raise, and management did not disclose plans.
Fairfax possibly raising its stake by 10%; management declined to comment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise resilience and capital adequacy, but evasive on fund raise, Fairfax stake and the income tax matter. Management was candid on the MTF decline and the cost pressure from employee expenses. Several answers were rough or deferred because of audio issues.
key_quotes: So I think we are running a profitable franchise, and we have enough we are -- all the cash is being used to reinvest in the business.
There won't be any material adverse impact on the financial position of the group.
As and when we have something very definitive, we will make all appropriate disclosures to the stock exchange as per regulatory guidelines.
